name.basis: The firm's own brand on bvp.com (the page title and the header logo's label). The adviser's legal name is Deer Management Co. LLC, primary business name 'BESSEMER VENTURE PARTNERS' (Form ADV Item 1, CRD 159279, SEC 801-125875, amendment of 2026-05-13). The general partners are the Deer VI to Deer XII & Co. entities; Bessemer Securities, Bessemer Trust and Lindsay Goldberg & Bessemer are separate businesses (decisions.md D3).

investor_type.basis: A venture capital firm investing through its own funds (54 private funds on Schedule D Section 7.B.(1) of its Form ADV, CRD 159279). Outside investors since Bessemer Venture Partners VII (2007); until then the money came from the Phipps family and Bessemer Securities (Wikipedia, 'Bessemer Venture Partners').

website.basis: The firm's own site, read 2026-10-06; bvp.com has been its one domain since the 1990s (config.json wayback).

founding_year.basis: 1981 is the year the firm itself came into being. Its own About page timeline (the Sanity aboutPage document, read 2026-10-06): '1981: The high-risk, high-growth investment group operating within the family office formally spins out into an independent venture firm: Bessemer Venture Partners.' COLLECTION.md s11 has every profile field answer a question about the firm, and the firm on this page is the adviser and fund family of decisions.md D1; Bessemer Securities, the family office, is a separate business that still exists and is outside that boundary (D3). The same reading as IVP (1980, not the 1974 of its predecessor) and ICONIQ Growth (2013, not ICONIQ's 2011). THE OTHER YEAR IS 1911: the timeline starts with 'Henry Phipps establishes a family office, which he names Bessemer Securities', and the firm has long presented that history as its own: a partner's biography in a portfolio company's proxy statements calls it 'the nation's oldest venture capital firm' (infoUSA, DEF 14A of 2001-04-20 and 2002-03-29, in sources/edgar/fts-hits.json), and its 2019 growth post says 'Since the formation of our fund nearly a century ago'. Wikipedia starts the firm's history in 1911 too and gives the spin-out no year ('Eventually the venture capital investment operation of Bessemer Securities was spun out'); the firm's own date is used. The history sentence on the page names both years. Intermediate dates: Pete Bancroft joined in 1967 'to lead the venture practice' (the firm's 2008 history page) and the California office opened in 1976. Flagged for a ruling, with decisions.md X1 (positions from before the spin-out).

investment_concept.basis: The hero headline (the page's h1) of the firm's homepage, 'Forged in steel. / Building what's next.', read 2026-10-06 on the live page and in the Sanity homePage document (sources/site/sanity/homePage.json, hero.headline); set on one line with a straight apostrophe and published in quotation marks as the firm's own words. Competing lines on the same page: the hero subhead, 'We exist to back audacious founders through dedicated early and growth practices.', which says more about what the firm does but is not the line it leads with (the rule takes the homepage headline first); and the meta description, which says the firm is 'Global in reach and decentralized by design' and 'backs founders in any sector', 'from seed to growth and beyond', 'with any check size'. The title tag is the firm's name alone.

history.value: Bessemer Venture Partners grew out of Bessemer Securities, the family office Henry Phipps founded in New York in 1911, and became an independent venture firm in 1981. The bets that made it were Staples, Ciena, VeriSign and Skype, followed by LinkedIn, Yelp, Shopify, Twilio, Pinterest, Toast and Anthropic. In September 2026 it raised $5.75 billion, $1.75 billion for early-stage companies and $4 billion for growth; the track record on this page leaves out its buyout arm, BVP Forge.
history.basis: Founding: the firm's own About page timeline (read 2026-10-06): '1911: Henry Phipps establishes a family office, which he names Bessemer Securities in honor of the Bessemer process' and '1981: ... formally spins out into an independent venture firm: Bessemer Venture Partners'. New York: the firm's 2008 history page (http://www.bvp.com/port/onepage.asp, Common Crawl capture of 2008-11-20, sources/site/history-narrative.json), 'Bessemer initially operated out of offices on Park Avenue, co-located with Bessemer Securities, its primary limited partner', and Wikipedia. The bets, each a verified portfolio company with the firm's own account of it: Staples ('invested in each of the company's four rounds, starting in 1986'), Ciena ('David Cowan invested for Bessemer in the B round'), VeriSign ('David Cowan co-founded the company in 1995 as a spin-out from RSA') and Skype (Rob Stavis 'led the A round'), all four on the 2008 history page; LinkedIn (memo of 2006-12-11, leading the Series C with $12.5 million), Yelp (memo of 2005-10-03), Shopify (memo of 2010-10-12, the Series A), Twilio (memo of 2009-11-06, a $125,000 seed cheque), Pinterest (memo of 2011-04-03, 'a term sheet to lead a $10m Series A'), Toast (memo of 2015-12-14, $17.5M of the $24M first institutional round), all at bvp.com/memos/<company>; Anthropic (posts of 2024-10-22, 'Why we backed Anthropic', and 2025-03-03, '$3.5 billion more for Anthropic'). The raise is the firm's post of 2026-09-22 (https://www.bvp.com/news/5-75-billion-to-back-the-founders-building-what-s-next): 'we're announcing $5.75 billion in new capital ... $1.75 billion for seed and early-stage investing and $4 billion for growth, raised in a single close'. The last clause is the portfolio boundary of decisions.md D2: BVP Forge, which the firm's timeline calls 'a private equity firm' (2022), buys majority or significant minority stakes and is outside the portfolio on this page. Moved to this sidecar, not the page: the Carnegie Steel origin (Phipps and Carnegie, 1872; the Bessemer process); Pete Bancroft leading the venture practice from 1967 and the Silicon Valley office of 1976; fund VII of 2007 as the first with outside investors (Wikipedia); the offices in Bangalore (2006), Tel Aviv (2007) and London (2021); the growth practice and the first Century fund (2019); the $1 billion AI commitment of 2023; the firm's own counts of '$20B' under management, '155+' IPOs and deSPACs and '450+' active portfolio companies (About page); the anti-portfolio; the fund ladder (funds field). 25 portfolio companies on this page date from before the 1981 spin-out and are in under the provisional reading of decisions.md X1.

INCLUDES BVP FORGE: $1,246,838,524 of that gross (6.2%) sits in the buyout strategy, which is outside the portfolio on this page (decisions.md D2, R5): BVP Forge Institutional, L.P. $595,271,408; BVP Forge Institutional A, L.P. $311,484,086; BVP Forge, L.P. $95,366,611; Gator Co-Invest LI, L.P. $70,885,000; Gator Co-Invest VE, L.P. $53,814,502; Gator Co-Invest BE, L.P. $45,189,577; Gator Co-Invest TE, L.P. $42,679,937; Gator Co-Invest PA, L.P. $32,147,403. funds.basis: 12 venture and growth funds from 2007 on, newest first: the numbered early-stage funds VII to XIII, the three Century growth funds and the two India funds. Each entry is a fund family (its L.P., Institutional, Parallel, feeder, Associates and Advisors & Influencers vehicles are parts of it, not rows). Sizes are the firm's own announcements from 2018 on and press before that, each with its source. FILING STYLE: since 2018 every Bessemer fund files Form D with an indefinite offering and $0 sold and does not amend, so no size can be asserted against a filing and NO entry carries an accession; the only filings with an amount sold are single vehicles of VIII ($885,000,000 and $615,100,000) and IX ($711,000,000), which corroborate those funds without showing the full size. THE 2026 MAPPING IS INFERRED: the firm's post gives '$1.75 billion for seed and early-stage investing' and '$4 billion for growth' and names no fund; XIII and Century Fund III are the two fund families it filed for on 2026-09-14. NOT LISTED: BVP Forge ($780 million, 2022, https://www.bvp.com/news/bvp-forge-raises-780-million-inaugural-fund) and BVP Forge II ($1 billion, closed 2025-11, https://www.bvp.com/news/bvp-forge-closes-1-billion-forge-ii), the buyout strategy, outside the portfolio on this page (decisions.md D2), and the five Gator Co-Invest vehicles, which are Forge's (R5); Bessemer Venture Partners VI (about 2004), whose size is not confirmed by any source read (the $296.9 million an aggregator gives is the gross asset value of the VI vehicle on the 2026 Form ADV, not a fund size); the 2009 annex fund, $350 million by the headline of Venture Capital Journal, 2009-02-26 (https://www.venturecapitaljournal.com/bessemer-venture-partners-raises-350-million-annex-fund/; the body is behind a registration wall), read as BVP VII Special Opportunity Fund L.P. investment_stage.basis: The firm's own two practices, crosswalked. Homepage (read 2026-10-06): 'We exist to back audacious founders through dedicated early and growth practices' and 'With two dedicated practices, seed/early and growth'; the meta description says 'from seed to growth and beyond'. Seed is Seed, early is Series A (the firm's early-stage funds lead first institutional rounds), growth is Growth. The fund architecture agrees: numbered early-stage funds beside the Century growth funds since 2019, and in 2026 '$1.75 billion for seed and early-stage investing and $4 billion for growth'. The site's own per-company stage field is not used: it reads 'seed' on 500 of 534 companies, a default of the site's migration (decisions.md D9). Reconciled with the landed entry stages over the 950 verified members: undetermined 346, Growth 244, Series A 238, Seed 119, Pre-Seed 3; entries dated 2019 or later: Growth 103, Series A 92, Seed 76, undetermined 40, Pre-Seed 3. All three stages appear. Of the 604 entries whose round the record gives, 360 (59.6%) are early (Pre-Seed, Seed or Series A) and the rest Growth, against the firm's own 'Roughly 70 percent of our investments are made at the early stage' (post of 2026-09-22). The two are not the same measure: the share here counts companies by the round the firm entered and reads every secondary, tender and later round as Growth. The undetermined share is mostly the era before the record names rounds.

investment_geo.basis: Derived from the portfolio's headquarters and reconciled with the firm's own words. The firm's About page says 'We invest wherever great companies are being built' and lists offices in Silicon Valley, San Francisco, Boston, New York, Westchester, Bangalore, Tel Aviv and London; its portfolio filter has four regions, on the 534 listed companies: us 410, israel 56, india 51, europe 24 (the region is the Bessemer team's, so its Canadian companies read 'us'). Headquarters: US 740 of the 950 verified members with a known country (77.9%); India 61 (6.4%); Israel 58 (6.1%); Europe 52 (5.5%); Canada 19 (2.0%); Oceania 5 (0.5%); China 4 (0.4%); Latin America 3 (0.3%); Southeast Asia 2 (0.2%); Europe by country: GB 28, DE 7, FR 4, NL 3, CH 2, DK 2, SE 2, BE 1, EE 1, LU 1, ES 1. A region is published at 2% of those members or more, most companies first. Core is the US alone: the core carries at most two labels (COLLECTION.md s1) and India and Israel, each with its own office and a like share, have an equal claim to the second, so neither is promoted. Entries dated 2019 or later: US 210, IN 28, IL 28, CA 11, GB 10, DE 7, AU 3, FR 3. Published on the 2% rule although not a region of the firm's own filter: Canada.

investment_scope.basis: focus from the firm's own site sector tags on 787 base rows, crosswalked to data/taxonomy/focus.json (crosswalk in config.json), published above 30 companies. Scope type is the curated judgement carried in investor.json.

investment_range.basis: MEDIAN: $15.7M, the median entry round over the 178 verified members whose entry round is on a Form D (p10 $3.5M, p25 $7.5M, p75 $30.0M, p90 $60.0M), published as $16.0M. It is a round size, not a cheque size, fair only for a lead investor with high ownership; electronic Form D starts in 2009 (17 of the rounds are from that year) and many recent companies file none. LOWER: $1,000,000, the firm's own words. Growth post of 2019-10-08 (https://www.bvp.com/news/bessemer-growth): 'Each of our partners now has the decision-making autonomy to support founders with their first $1 million or their last $250 million check'; the fund X post of 2018-10-25 has 'their first $1 million (or $50,000) as well as support growth-stage companies with a $100 million check'. A firm statement is taken as the floor as on Insight Partners and Menlo Ventures (COLLECTION.md s11: programme floors give the lower limit; the firm runs no seed programme with a published cheque size). Smaller cheques are on the record and are not the published floor: the '(or $50,000)' of 2018, and the $125,000 seed cheque into Twilio (memo of 2009-11-06). The p10 entry round, $3.5M, is the proxy it replaces. UPPER: $450,000,000, the largest round the firm led in the last five years, the Series A of Inertia Enterprises ('Bessemer Venture Partners leads Inertia Enterprises $450M Series A to bring proven fusion science to the grid.', the firm's post of 2026-02-11, https://www.bvp.com/news/powering-the-future-the-path-to-commercial-fusion-energy-with-inertia-enterprises; a verified portfolio company). It is the round, not the firm's cheque, which is undisclosed (the post calls the investment 'milestone-based'): at a 10 to 15% single position the largest fund, Century Fund III at $4.00B, supports $400.0M to $600.0M, so the figure is inside what the funds support. The firm's own ceiling in words is older and lower: 'their last $250 million check' (2019). Other rounds it led alone, from the portfolio's round records: Upwind $250.0M (Series B, 2026-01); Klook $210.0M (Series E+, 2023-12); Legora $150.0M (Series C, 2025-10); Onyx Security $113.0M (Series B, 2026-07); Teleport $110.0M (Series C, 2022-05). Not used, because the firm did not lead alone: EliseAI $350M (co-led), Waymo $16B (joined), Anthropic $3.5B (took part). REJECTED: 'with any check size' (meta description), a slogan with no figure.

notable_investments.basis: The five best known of the verified portfolio companies to a general reader, most recognised first (COLLECTION.md s11, PRO-152), each with the firm's own account of its entry: LinkedIn (memo of 2006, leading the Series C), Pinterest (memo of 2011, leading the $10M Series A), Shopify (memo of 2010, the Series A), Skype (the A round, the firm's 2008 history page) and Twitch (memo of 2012, leading the Series B). Fame is the model's judgement, the one licensed use of it. Next in line, left out by the cap of five: Anthropic, Canva, Yelp, Staples, Waymo, Wix, DocuSign, Twilio, Toast; the history names several of them.

flags.note: Published 1981, the year the venture group left Bessemer Securities and became Bessemer Venture Partners (the firm's own timeline). The firm also claims 1911, the year the family office was set up, and Wikipedia starts the firm's history there. The history names both years. Rule which year the page should carry; it is the same seam as decisions.md X1 (25 companies from before 1981 are in provisionally).

Both ends are the one sworn figure, $20,239,213,324 (Item 5.F, 2026-05-13). It includes $1,246,838,524 of gross assets (6.2% of the 7.B roster) in BVP Forge and its Gator Co-Invest vehicles, the buyout strategy that is outside the portfolio on this page; without them the venture and growth funds hold about $19.01B gross. Item 5.F cannot be split, so rule whether the whole figure stands. It is also a floor: the $5.75 billion of September 2026 and Forge II are not in it. The 7.B roster sums to $20,260,011,961, $20,798,637 off Item 5.F.

The 2026 mapping is inferred: the firm's post gives $1.75 billion for seed and early stage and $4 billion for growth and names no fund; XIII and Century Fund III are the fund families it filed for on 2026-09-14. No fund carries an accession (Bessemer files indefinite offerings with $0 sold). Left out: fund VI (size not confirmed), the 2009 annex fund ($350 million by a headline; that it is BVP VII Special Opportunity Fund is inferred), BVP Forge and Forge II (outside the portfolio). IX rests on FinSMEs as the research read it; the page refused a second read.

The ceiling, $450,000,000, is the size of a round the firm led (Inertia Enterprises, Series A), not a cheque; the largest fund supports $400.0M to $600.0M at 10 to 15%, and the firm's own words stop at a '$250 million check' (2019). The lower limit, $1 million, is the firm's stated first cheque; its 2018 post adds '(or $50,000)' and its Twilio memo records a $125,000 seed cheque, so rule whether the smallest stated figure should stand instead. The median, $16.0M, is a Form D round-size proxy over 178 of 950 companies.

Published at 30 companies or more. DISAGREEMENT, flagged and not overwritten (COLLECTION.md s11): 'AI' is a tag the firm puts across its whole list ('AI is reshaping every one of them', homepage), so it leads here while the per-company focus puts far fewer companies in AI; 'Vertical' and 'Enterprise', the firm's two software practices, both land in SaaS; and the firm's vocabulary has no sector for Media, Gaming & Advertising 49, Climate & Energy 20, Crypto & Web3 4 (per-company counts), the Lightspeed signal. The per-company focus over the verified members reads: SaaS 155, Data Infrastructure 139, Healthcare & Bio 119, Consumer & Marketplaces 118, Industrial & Robotics 83, AI & Applied AI 72, Security 69, Fintech & Payments 69, Media, Gaming & Advertising 49, DevTools & APIs 29, Climate & Energy 20, Crypto & Web3 4. Generalist: the firm says it 'backs founders in any sector' (meta description) and no sector carries the portfolio.

All three stages appear. Of the 604 entries whose round the record gives, 360 (59.6%) are early (Pre-Seed, Seed or Series A) and the rest Growth, against the firm's own 'Roughly 70 percent of our investments are made at the early stage' (post of 2026-09-22). The two are not the same measure: the share here counts companies by the round the firm entered and reads every secondary, tender and later round as Growth.
Core is the US alone under the two-label cap; India and Israel have an equal claim to a second core label. Canada is published on the 2% rule and is not a region of the firm's own filter.
Fame is a judgement: LinkedIn, Pinterest, Shopify, Skype and Twitch are published; Anthropic, Canva, Yelp and Staples are the nearest alternatives. Skype shut down in 2025.

The firm counts '155+' IPOs and deSPACs and '450+' active portfolio companies (About page); the portfolio on this page records a public listing for 98 of its 950 companies. The gap is not explained here; listing data is thinner for the older companies (decisions.md D8). Neither count is on the page.

The shared rule publishes Larchmont, NY. The Form ADV principal office is Larchmont, NY, and the firm's contact page lists that office among its own, so the site agrees. No override is set: an override is for a flaw in the reading, never a preference, and the reading has none. What a reviewer may still rule on: the same filing counts advisory staff at the other offices (New York, NY 29, Redwood City, CA 16, Bangalore, India 12, San Francisco, CA 8, Wellesley, MA 8, Cambridge, MA 6, Tel Aviv-Yafo, Israel 5, London, United Kingdom 3, Ebene, Mauritius 1; 88 in all, against 83 firm-wide in Item 5.B.(1), so some are counted at two offices) and gives no count for the principal office; Wikipedia calls the firm 'headquartered in San Francisco'; and the site lists Silicon Valley first and labels no headquarters. A recorded site statement (config.json profile.site_office) needs the firm's own words, and none were found.
